claims.text: An MTP trained specifically on liquid-state configurations of Ta-based BCC HEAs can replace full thermodynamic integration with a targeted perturbation scheme.
The proposed method will reproduce DFT thermodynamic-integration melting free energies within 2%.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by more than 90%.
Including high-temperature liquid snapshots in the training set prevents solid-state-bias artifacts.
Ta-W-Cr-V alloys can be represented on a BCC lattice.
The relevant Ta-based alloy is a disordered BCC solid solution at temperatures approaching melting.
Standard experimental melting measurements are infeasible for the stated Ta-based HEAs.
Sampling only near the solid-liquid coexistence line is sufficient to avoid integration over the full solid-to-liquid phase-space path.
The solid-liquid transition of the proposed Ta-based alloys lies approximately between 2000 and 3000 K.
A training set containing at least 20% liquid configurations generated by AIMD at 1.5 times the estimated melting temperature is adequate for the proposed MTP.
AIMD can provide liquid-state density or configuration data for multicomponent HEAs under a zero-pressure target.
The MTP will accurately reproduce local coordination-number distributions and bond-angle distortions in the multicomponent liquid.
Standard EAM potentials fail to reproduce the complex liquid structure of multicomponent HEAs.
Accurate MTP descriptions of liquid entropy and enthalpy near coexistence permit the free-energy difference to be estimated using only a small number of sampling windows.
The calculated melting temperature will differ by less than 50 K from a DFT thermodynamic-integration reference.
The MTP will reduce computational time per configuration by a factor of 100 relative to AIMD.
The resulting speedup will enable high-throughput screening of Ta-based HEA compositions.
A W-Ta-Cr-V alloy exhibits a strong segregation tendency involving Cr and V and can form a Cr-V-rich precipitate.
The method may fail when the liquid exhibits extreme chemical segregation or polyatomic clusters absent from the training data.
Extrapolation errors in liquid density are a failure mode of machine-learning potentials in multicomponent spaces.

contradictions.description: The proposed accuracy is conditioned on training specifically for the Ta-based HEA using system-specific liquid AIMD data, whereas the principal blind test uses a composition absent from the training set. That test evaluates cross-composition transferability rather than the explicitly proposed composition-specific workflow.
